question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following statements about a Cat III AIF's constitutional structure is INCORRECT?

answer.text: A Cat III AIF can be constituted as a trust, LLP, company, or statutory body corporate
A Cat III AIF can be either open-ended or close-ended
A Cat III AIF scheme must have minimum corpus of INR 20 crore
A Cat III AIF CAN exceed the 1,000 investor cap by treating additional non-accredited investors as 'guests' for a limited window

explanation.text: The Logic: The 1,000-investor cap is a hard regulatory ceiling for non-accredited investors in a scheme. There is no 'guest' concept or temporary exception. Accredited investors (Accredited Investors under AI framework) are EXCLUDED from the count — that's the only way to exceed 1,000 total. Options A, B, C are all correct; only D is fabricated. The Trap: Option D is the fabricated exception — the other three are textbook correct. When a 'negative-framed' question appears, identify the odd-out carefully. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D all test these same constitutional constraints. Manager's Pro-Tip: Your compliance calendar should have an automatic alert at 950 non-accredited investors — this buys time to onboard as AIs, launch a parallel scheme, or pause subscriptions before hitting 1,000.
